answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a verifier’s score is the walk’s probability mass reaching each agent. A Sybil cluster isolated by few cross-attestations has low conductance, so escape probability—and thus imported trust—stays small under min-cut transitivity bounds. Hence its aggregate voting weight cannot scale with internal size, even if it presents timber, pearl, and harbor identities.
